packs.name: Quick Start
packs.description: Standard Turbo model with full pipeline — ready to generate in minutes. Best for most users.

packs.name: Minimal Setup
packs.description: Smallest viable setup — great for low-VRAM GPUs or quick testing.

packs.name: XL Quality
packs.description: XL Turbo model — larger architecture for richer, more detailed audio. Needs ~12GB VRAM.

packs.name: Blackwell Optimized
packs.description: MXFP4 quantised XL — native FP4 Tensor Core acceleration on RTX 5000 series. 22% faster than Q4.

packs.name: CUDA 13 Runtime
packs.description: NVIDIA CUDA 13.x runtime libraries required for GPU-accelerated generation. ~510 MB download.

packs.name: CUDA 12 Runtime
packs.description: NVIDIA CUDA 12.x runtime libraries for the CUDA 12.8 compatibility build. ~810 MB download.

packs.name: MiniMax-Music3 (F16)
packs.description: All five MiniMax-Music3 components at full precision — the reference quality bar. ~24 GB download.

packs.name: MiniMax-Music3 (Q8_0)
packs.description: LM, DiT and depth decoder at Q8_0 with the frontends near-native — near-lossless, about half the size and a faster LM step. Recommended. ~13 GB download.

packs.name: MiniMax-Music3 (Balanced mix)
packs.description: The split format's point: LM at Q8_0 (quality lives in the language model) with the DiT at Q4_K_M (VRAM lives in the flow stack), depth at Q8_0, frontends near-native. ~12 GB download.

packs.name: MiniMax-Music3 (Q6_K)
packs.description: LM and DiT at Q6_K, depth at Q8_0 (its validated floor), frontends near-native. ~10 GB download.

packs.name: MiniMax-Music3 (Q4_K_M)
packs.description: LM and DiT at Q4_K_M, depth at Q8_0, frontends near-native — the compact option for limited VRAM. ~8 GB download.

packs.name: MiniMax-Music3 (NVFP4)
packs.description: LM and DiT at NVFP4 — the FASTEST option measured (~18 ms/frame in the autoregressive stage vs ~117 for the K-quants) using Blackwell (RTX 50-series) native FP4 kernels; depth at Q8_0, frontends near-native. Quality is not yet judged by ear. ~8 GB download.

packs.name: MiniMax-Music3 Training
packs.description: Everything the Training Studio needs to train an MM3 artist adapter, on top of a generation pack. The two encoders turn your audio into codes; the F16 depth decoder is the one the trainer requires (the quantised depth files shipped with the generation packs are for generation only).

packs.name: MM3 TensorRT DiT
packs.description: The native TensorRT renderer for the MM3 Flow DiT: the ONNX graph plus the two core TensorRT runtime DLLs (nvinfer, ONNX parser). Weights are refit from whichever DiT GGUF you already have selected — this does not replace it. You also need ONE builder resource DLL matching your GPU's compute capability (SM); pick it separately in the TensorRT section of the Model Manager, since it depends on hardware this pack can't know in advance.

packs.name: Stem Separation
packs.description: All 4 models for multi-stem audio separation in Cover Studio. Required for the SuperSep pipeline.

packs.name: StableStep Separation (Leap Xe)
packs.description: BS-Roformer-Leap Xe vocal + instrumental pair for the StableStep pipeline. Native GGML — does NOT need the Stem Separation Runtime. ~510 MB.

packs.name: Stem Separation Runtime
packs.description: ONNX Runtime + cuDNN libraries required to run SuperSep stem separation on GPU. ~1.3 GB download.

packs.name: Local Captioning (MOSS)
packs.description: Caption your own tracks locally in the Training Studio — MOSS listens to the audio instead of rewriting text. Also emits MM3 Structured Captions.

packs.name: YuE2 Recommended
packs.description: YuE2 — a second generation backend, separate from ACE-Step and MiniMax-Music3: an autoregressive language model (plan/semantic/nar stages) plus a VAE decoder, producing 48 kHz stereo audio from a freeform style + lyrics prompt. Q8_0 LM (near-lossless, NAR-stage rel-L2 vs bf16 output 0.019 against bf16's own 0.013 baseline — docs/plans/yue2/07-quant-ladder.md §5) plus the standard VAE. ~4.4 GB total. License: CC BY-NC 4.0 (non-commercial) — free for personal and research use, but not for commercial products. For a commercial license, contact the upstream authors at gezhang@umich.edu.

packs.name: YuE2 Full Precision
packs.description: YuE2 at source precision (BF16 LM) plus the standard VAE — the reference quality bar the whole quant ladder is measured against (docs/plans/yue2/07-quant-ladder.md). Largest download and VRAM footprint of the four YuE2 packs. ~7.8 GB total. License: CC BY-NC 4.0 (non-commercial) — free for personal and research use, but not for commercial products. For a commercial license, contact the upstream authors at gezhang@umich.edu.

packs.name: YuE2 Compact (imatrix)
packs.description: YuE2 with the Q4_K_M-imat LM (imatrix-guided quantization; NAR-stage rel-L2 vs bf16 output 0.116 against bf16's own 0.013 baseline — docs/plans/yue2/07-quant-ladder.md §12/§14) plus the standard VAE. The usual choice for limited VRAM. ~3.0 GB total. License: CC BY-NC 4.0 (non-commercial) — free for personal and research use, but not for commercial products. For a commercial license, contact the upstream authors at gezhang@umich.edu.

packs.name: YuE2 Tiny (imatrix)
packs.description: YuE2 with the smallest LM this ladder ships, Q2_K-imat, plus the standard VAE. WARNING: audibly degraded — NAR-stage rel-L2 vs bf16 output is 0.389 against bf16's own 0.013 baseline (docs/plans/yue2/07-quant-ladder.md §12/§14), the second-worst measurement on the whole ladder. Pick this only for the smallest possible download/VRAM footprint and expect the flow-matching output to sound rougher than every other pack. ~2.2 GB total. License: CC BY-NC 4.0 (non-commercial) — free for personal and research use, but not for commercial products. For a commercial license, contact the upstream authors at gezhang@umich.edu.

packs.name: YuE2 Minted Regulariser Pack
packs.description: Optional training data for YuE2 artist (AR) LoRAs: mixes true YuE2 semantic codes into training so the adapter does not collapse into the encoder's adjacent-repeat defect. Not needed for generation, or for the NAR adapter trainer. About 91 MB.

packs.name: YuE2 Artist (AR) Training Pack
packs.description: Everything ace-train needs to train a YuE2 artist adapter beyond the base LM: the semantic tokenizer that writes the codec targets the AR learns to predict, the MMS_FA aligner behind the lyric-cursor loss, and the minted regulariser. Training only - none of it is needed to generate.

MiniMax-Music3 language model in its source BF16 precision, for TRAINING adapters with BF16 tensor cores: pick it as the base in the MM3 train form and the trainer runs the projection GEMMs on the tensor cores instead of the F32 fallback. Measured 1.4x faster per step than q8_0 on a 5090 at matched crop, for about 9 GB more VRAM (needs a 40 GB+ card at the default crop). Same 17.2 GB as F16; not better than F16 for generation, where q8_0 is the pick.

MiniMax-Music3 autoregressive language model — generates the semantic/acoustic token sequence from the Structured Caption. Full precision. The reference quality bar. Both mm3-lm and mm3-synth are required; this file is ~17.2 GB.

MiniMax-Music3 autoregressive language model — generates the semantic/acoustic token sequence from the Structured Caption. Near-lossless and roughly twice as fast on the LM step. The recommended default. Both mm3-lm and mm3-synth are required; this file is ~9.1 GB.

MiniMax-Music3 autoregressive language model — generates the semantic/acoustic token sequence from the Structured Caption. Very close to q8_0 quality at a smaller footprint. NOTE: measured 5-6x slower than Q8_0 or NVFP4 in the autoregressive stage on CUDA — pick NVFP4 or Q8_0 for speed. Both mm3-lm and mm3-synth are required; this file is ~7.1 GB. Quantized against an importance matrix collected from the f16 model, which is what makes the low-bit builds usable: the solver spends its error budget on the weights that carry signal instead of spreading it evenly.

Includes the depth decoder, condition encoder, flow DiT and vocoder. Smallest and lowest quality. Experimental — the flow model may not hold up. Both mm3-lm and mm3-synth are required; this file is ~1.4 GB.

MiniMax-Music3 condition encoder (~25M) — fuses the AR stage's hidden states into the DiT's conditioning track. Never quantised (bandwidth-bound frontend); this f16 file serves every quant combination. Full precision — the reference quality bar. This file is ~0.1 GB.

MiniMax-Music3 RVQ depth decoder (0.6B) — predicts the 7 acoustic codebooks per frame inside the AR loop. Split-format file. Q8_0 is the validated floor for quality; sub-Q8 variants exist for experiments. 4-bit float, portable variant. Experimental. This file is ~0.4 GB.

MiniMax-Music3 RVQ depth decoder (0.6B) — predicts the 7 acoustic codebooks per frame inside the AR loop. Split-format file. Q8_0 is the validated floor for quality; sub-Q8 variants exist for experiments. 4-bit float, Blackwell-native kernels. Experimental. This file is ~0.4 GB.

MOSS-Music audio encoder — 32-layer Whisper-style tower plus the SwiGLU adapter and deepstack mergers that inject audio into the LM. F16 only, never quantised: the adapter output runs ~770x hotter than the encoder's, so quantisation error lands straight in the LM's input embeddings. Required by every moss-lm file; ~1.6 GB.

YuE2 autoregressive language model — plans the semantic/acoustic token sequence from a freeform style + lyrics prompt (plan/semantic/nar stages). Source precision — the reference quality bar the rest of the ladder below is measured against (NAR-stage rel-L2 0.013 vs its own output, docs/plans/yue2/07-quant-ladder.md §5). Required alongside one of the VAE decoders below; this file is ~7.3 GB. Non-commercial use only: YuE2's weights are licensed CC BY-NC 4.0. For a commercial license, contact the upstream authors at gezhang@umich.edu.

Turns real audio into YuE2 semantic tokens — the reverse of what the LM does. Optional, and only useful for training: with it, `ace-train yue2-tokenize` fills the codec_ids slot in a YuE2 preprocess cache so a NAR adapter trains on ground-truth codes exactly as inference conditions, instead of the text-only regime. Not needed to generate music. One file holds both halves of the chain: MERT-v2-FullSong's mel frontend, ConvNext subsampler and first 21 Conformer blocks, plus Mothersuperior's 8-layer tokenizer head (docs/plans/yue2/12-tokenizer-oracle-pin.md). Non-commercial use only: derived from YuE2-3B and licensed CC BY-NC 4.0. For a commercial license, contact the upstream authors at gezhang@umich.edu.

Meta's MMS forced aligner, converted to GGUF (CC BY-NC-4.0 upstream). Training-only: ace-train yue2-align uses it to write per-word lyric spans into the preprocess manifest, which is what the AR trainer's --cursor-weight supervises. F32 because the port's stage gates were measured in fp32. Not used at generation.

Manifest half of the minted regulariser pack for AR LoRA training (ace-train yue2-ar-train --minted): 4,732 songs, 216 held out as minted_val. Converted from Mothersuperior/yue2-minted-corpus (CC BY-NC-4.0). The trainer resolves the codes blob RELATIVE TO THIS FILE, so it must sit beside minted_codes.i32. Without the pack the trainer needs --allow-no-minted and trains artist-only, which the encoder's adjacent-repeat defect makes a bad trade.
Codes half of the minted regulariser pack: true YuE2 semantic codes as headerless little-endian int32, indexed by minted_manifest.json. Not useful alone.
Best balance of speed and accuracy (1.5 GB). Recommended. ~5-10s per 30s track on GPU.
Maximum accuracy (2.9 GB). Slower but best for difficult transcriptions. ~10-20s per 30s track on GPU.
Good accuracy with lower VRAM usage (1.4 GB). ~3-8s per 30s track on GPU.
Fastest, smallest (141 MB). Good for quick previews but lower accuracy. ~1-3s per 30s track on GPU.

MiniMax-Music3 autoregressive language model, quantized to IQ2_XXS (2.06 bits per weight) against an importance matrix — the smallest build that still holds together. The IQ formats cannot be built without one at all, and it is what makes them listenable rather than a curiosity. Note they decode through a codebook lookup rather than a simple scale, so they are slower per token on CPU than a K-quant of the same size; pick them for a memory ceiling, not for speed.

MiniMax-Music3 autoregressive language model, quantized to IQ3_XXS (3.06 bits per weight) against an importance matrix — between Q2_K and Q3_K_S on size, and better than either at it. The IQ formats cannot be built without one at all, and it is what makes them listenable rather than a curiosity. Note they decode through a codebook lookup rather than a simple scale, so they are slower per token on CPU than a K-quant of the same size; pick them for a memory ceiling, not for speed.

MiniMax-Music3 autoregressive language model, quantized to IQ2_XS (2.31 bits per weight) against an importance matrix — a little more headroom than IQ2_XXS. The IQ formats cannot be built without one at all, and it is what makes them listenable rather than a curiosity. Note they decode through a codebook lookup rather than a simple scale, so they are slower per token on CPU than a K-quant of the same size; pick them for a memory ceiling, not for speed.

MiniMax-Music3 autoregressive language model, quantized to IQ4_XS (4.25 bits per weight) against an importance matrix — Q4-class quality at slightly under Q4_K_S size. The IQ formats cannot be built without one at all, and it is what makes them listenable rather than a curiosity. Note they decode through a codebook lookup rather than a simple scale, so they are slower per token on CPU than a K-quant of the same size; pick them for a memory ceiling, not for speed.

Audio → RVQ codes. TRAINING ONLY — the Training Studio's MM3 codes stage needs this to turn your dataset's audio into the code streams the LM trains on; generation never loads it. MiniMax never released the official tokenizer, so this is PurpleOrc's open-rvq encoder (169M, SimpleTuner v4 architecture, trained from scratch on a 53k-track multilingual corpus), converted to GGUF. Codes are encoder-specific: an adapter trained on these codes must keep using this encoder. This file is ~0.7 GB.

Audio → LM frame hiddens. TRAINING ONLY, and OPTIONAL: powers the codes stage's "Cover-launder" option, which renders each track back through the model before encoding so buried vocals reach the code targets — the ear-validated fix for dense-mix artists. PurpleOrc's rec7 encoder (170M, MIT) converted to GGUF, with the MM3 LM's two semantic table slices baked in so laundering never runs the 8B language model. Skip it if you never use laundered codes.

The frozen half of every HOT-PiZZA / PiSSA adapter trained on the Q8_0 language model at rank 128: the base weights' own top-128 singular directions, shipped once instead of inside each adapter. Needed to LOAD any MM3 artist adapter trained from 2026-09-09 on (the adapter files are 0.7 GB instead of 2.8 GB because of it) and read by the trainer so new adapters export in that form. Generation without an adapter does not use it. This file is ~0.7 GB.

MiniMax-Music3 DAV audio encoder — 44.1 kHz stereo into the 128-channel flow latents. TRAINING ONLY: it is the input stage of the Training Studio's MM3 codes job, paired with the RVQ encoder. Generation does not use it. This file is ~0.1 GB.

The MiniMax-Music3 Flow DiT exported as a TensorRT graph — network structure only, no meaningful weights of its own. On first use per GPU, the engine builds a GPU- and TensorRT-version-specific engine from this graph (one time, a few minutes; cached under models/mm3/mm3-trt-cache/). Every weight is then refit at load time from whichever DiT GGUF quant you already have selected (F16/F32 direct, quantized ones dequantized on the fly), so installing this does not replace your DiT choice. Needs the TensorRT runtime entries below — the core pair plus the ONE builder resource DLL matching your GPU's compute capability (SM); without those TensorRT stays unavailable and generation falls back to the GGML renderer.
NVIDIA TensorRT core inference library. Required for the MM3 TensorRT DiT renderer; ace-server links it with delayed loading, so its absence only disables TensorRT (the GGML renderer keeps working).
NVIDIA TensorRT's ONNX parser. Required alongside the core TensorRT runtime to build the MM3 DiT engine from mm3-dit-trt.onnx on first use.

TensorRT's engine-builder resource for compute capability 7.5 (Turing — RTX 20-series, GTX 16-series, T4). Needed only on first use per GPU, to build the MM3 DiT TensorRT engine; pick the ONE matching your card, not all of them.

TensorRT's engine-builder resource for compute capability 8.0 (Ampere datacenter — A100). Needed only on first use per GPU, to build the MM3 DiT TensorRT engine; pick the ONE matching your card, not all of them.

TensorRT's engine-builder resource for compute capability 8.6 (Ampere — RTX 30-series, A40). Needed only on first use per GPU, to build the MM3 DiT TensorRT engine; pick the ONE matching your card, not all of them.

TensorRT's engine-builder resource for compute capability 8.9 (Ada Lovelace — RTX 40-series, L4/L40). Needed only on first use per GPU, to build the MM3 DiT TensorRT engine; pick the ONE matching your card, not all of them.

TensorRT's engine-builder resource for compute capability 9.0 (Hopper — H100). Needed only on first use per GPU, to build the MM3 DiT TensorRT engine; pick the ONE matching your card, not all of them.

TensorRT's engine-builder resource for compute capability 10.0 (Blackwell datacenter — B100/B200). Needed only on first use per GPU, to build the MM3 DiT TensorRT engine; pick the ONE matching your card, not all of them.

TensorRT's engine-builder resource for compute capability 12.0 (Blackwell consumer — RTX 50-series). Needed only on first use per GPU, to build the MM3 DiT TensorRT engine; pick the ONE matching your card, not all of them.

TensorRT's PTX-JIT builder resource — compiles at engine-build time for whatever compute capability the specific SM DLLs above don't cover (a newer GPU than this release shipped for). Slower to build than a matching SM DLL, but works on anything CUDA can target. Use this only if none of the numbered SM entries match your GPU.
